issues.detail: The Hebrew 'אַתָּה עַתָּה תַּעֲשֶׂה מְלוּכָה עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל' is a rhetorical statement: 'You now exercise kingship over Israel' (i.e., you are king, so act like it). The Vietnamese renders it as a question 'Ông có thực sự đang cai trị vương quốc Y-sơ-ra-ên không?' ('Are you really ruling the kingdom of Israel?'), which changes the meaning from an assertion to a doubting question, altering the force and content of the verse.

The Hebrew 'הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִי' refers to Naboth as 'the Jezreelite' (from Jezreel). The Vietnamese renders it as 'người Y-xơ-ra-en' ('the Israelite'), swapping the place name Jezreel for Israel, which changes the identity of Naboth.
